author: CBR
description:
The Boys, Invincible and Watchmen prove superhero deconstruction works because they treat absolute power as psychological horror, political reality, and human tragedy.

In this video, Tim McDonald breaks down why the best superhero adaptations often are not traditional MCU stories at all. Instead of protecting their icons, The Boys, Invincible, Watchmen, Spider-Verse, and M. Night Shyamalan’s Unbreakable trilogy force the genre to confront trauma, ideology, celebrity, violence, and state power. This superhero deconstruction argument goes beyond “dark and gritty” and asks what superheroes would actually do to people, institutions, and society.

You’ll see why Homelander feels like the ultimate product of fame without consequences, why Invincible makes collateral damage horrifying, why Spider-Verse understands comic-book form better than most live-action films, and why Unbreakable, Split, and Glass may be the boldest modern superhero trilogy. title: Why the Best Superhero Stories Aren’t in the MCU
